text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 10px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start

g.text: Colour each circuit neuron by its network and count
the networks, weighted by size: exp(entropy).
Fewer = more concentrated. The test: does a circuit
use fewer networks than random neurons drawn with the
same number per layer ("random sets", grey in the results)?

path.style: fill: #c44e52; opacity: 0.85; stroke: #e9a23b; stroke-width: 1.5; stroke-linejoin: miter

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 10px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start

g.text: b Do a domain's tasks reuse networks?
Choose networks on the other tasks of a domain,
then score the task that was left out.
→ share of task 1's circuit inside them
Every task is left out in turn. Ratio > 1: tasks of
a domain put their circuits into the same networks.

fill: #4c72b0; opacity: 0.35; stroke: #4c72b0; stroke-width: 1.5; stroke-linejoin: miter

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 10px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start

g.text: c Do overlapping tasks share networks?
Shared neurons are left out: they would be in
the same networks under any partition.
Across all task pairs: does more circuit overlap go
with more similar networks for the remaining neurons?
